ceramic.name: vessel
ceramic.title: vessel
ceramic.reason: A handmade earthenware vessel with rounded body, flared rim, and incised/burnished decoration—typical West African traditional pottery, consistent with Brong ceramic production and directly attributed by the museum to Brong makers.

ceramic.name: pot
ceramic.title: pot
ceramic.reason: A traditional multi-handled earthenware storage pot with stopper, attributed by the museum to Brong potters of Ghana; this is a typical handmade domestic ceramic form for the region.

ceramic.name: vessel
ceramic.title: vessel
ceramic.reason: A handmade burnished red-slip pottery vessel with narrow neck, a globular form consistent with traditional Akan/Brong pottery of Ghana, museum directly attributes it to Brong makers.

metalwork.name: vase
metalwork.title: vase
metalwork.reason: This is a metal (bronze/brass) pedestal vase with engraved animal decoration and handles, made by the Brong (Bono) people of Ghana — a piece metalworkers produced for domestic/ritual use, not a ceramic object.

metalwork.name: lamp
metalwork.title: lamp
metalwork.reason: A bronze tripod lamp with a bowl on a decorated stem, a documented Brong (Akan-related Ghanaian) metalworking tradition; museum attributes it directly to Brong makers, no caveat noted.

metalwork.name: Weight
metalwork.title: Mask gold weight
metalwork.reason: This is a classic Akan brass gold weight in the form of a human head/mask, a type made by Akan-related peoples including the Brong (Abron); the miniature face with incised scarification patterns matches known gold-weight production of this region.

metalwork.name: vessel
metalwork.title: vessel
metalwork.reason: This is a cast bronze/brass tripod vessel with small cast animal (bird and quadruped) figures around the rim and an incised chevron band — a form consistent with Akan-family kuduo-type ceremonial vessels, a known lost-wax casting tradition of Brong/Akan peoples in Ghana used for storing valuables and ritual use.

metalwork.name: lamp
metalwork.title: lamp
metalwork.reason: A bronze zoomorphic (bird-shaped) oil lamp with suspension chain, a form of cast metal utensil well attested among Akan-related groups in Ghana such as the Brong, used for household lighting.

masks-ritual.name: mask
masks-ritual.title: mask
masks-ritual.reason: A bronze mask with engraved decoration, attributed by the museum's ethnic production data to the Brong people of Ghana; metal masks with abstract facial features fit the region's ritual/masking traditions.
